observation_kind: 100 distinct official-source checks plus 12 exact-data blockers; each check is applied once to each of 3 preserved candidates; no validation-mode multiplication.
f: Current INSPIRE files were published on 5 July 2026.
New INSPIRE files are published on the first Sunday of each month.
London Borough of Haringey is listed in the current local-authority index.
INSPIRE polygons are downloaded by local authority.
A GIS is required to view the downloaded polygons.
Downloading the files accepts the stated OGL conditions.
INSPIRE is a subset of registered freehold land and property.
Polygons show indicative position and extent, not definitive legal extent.
Each polygon has a unique Land Registry INSPIRE ID.
The INSPIRE ID relates a polygon to a registered title.
The individual title plan is required to establish registered extent.
One registered title may contain several separate polygons.
Each separate polygon has its own INSPIRE ID.
A missing INSPIRE ID may indicate unregistered land or an excluded tenure.
GML is an open interoperable GIS/CAD data format.
GML can be converted to other GIS formats.
Converted data must use an appropriate projection.
QGIS can view and convert the supplied GML.
The catalogue identifies INSPIRE as free, monthly, OGL-licensed GML with no API.
The National Polygon Service is paid and API-enabled, so it is not substituted for free INSPIRE.
The API exposes more than 100 planning and housing datasets.
Datasets are exposed through one consistent interface.
Latitude and longitude return entities whose geometry intersects the point.
A request can include multiple dataset parameters.
Entities can include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point.
No result does not prove no constraint exists because coverage varies.
UPRN searches use the q parameter.
UPRN is more precise than a coordinate for registered properties.
All 337 local planning authorities can be fetched in one request.
geometry_entity can use an existing entity boundary.
Custom WKT geometry filters are supported.
Custom query geometry uses WGS84 coordinates.
Spatial relations include within, equals, disjoint, intersects, touches, contains, covers, coveredby, overlaps and crosses.
Large result sets use limit and offset pagination.
Responses can provide next, previous, first and last links.
The property-screening API has no batch endpoint.
Portfolio screening requires one request per property.
The field parameter limits returned fields.
exclude_field can remove fields when field is not used.
The quality parameter filters entity quality.
Bulk downloads provide a stable snapshot for local intersections.
Bulk formats include CSV, JSON, GeoJSON and Parquet where applicable.
The API is beta and may change for production integrations.
Entity search supports JSON, HTML and GeoJSON extensions.
Single-entity retrieval supports JSON, HTML and GeoJSON.
Dataset list and detail endpoints support JSON and HTML.
An official OpenAPI document is published.
The official coordinate example returned application/json.
The live example includes entities marked authoritative.
The live example includes WKT geometry and point fields.
Article 4 direction area reports 7,152 records and 112 providers.
Article 4 direction reports 3,175 records and 102 providers.
Article 4 publishing requires direction and direction-area datasets.
Direction-area geometry must be polygon or multipolygon in WGS84.
The composite DTM covers approximately 99% of England.
The composite has 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM uses the last or only laser return.
Surface objects are removed to model terrain.
The current composite was produced in 2022.
The composite combines Time Stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Repeated coverage uses the newest best-resolution survey.
Composite inputs span 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
Downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in 5 km OS-grid tiles.
Heights are metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15.
Input surveys have ±15 cm RMSE vertical accuracy.
The coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The dataset update frequency is annual.
The dataset is OGL licensed with no public access constraint.
WMS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API Features services are listed.
WCS is supported at OGC version 2.0.1.
WCS can return raw elevation pixel values.
A persistent no-year WCS endpoint is documented.
Published DTM1 stretch statistics include min, max, mean and standard deviation.
OGC services replace proprietary Esri image services.
GeoTIFF storage was reported as about five times smaller than ASCII.
Time Stamped DSM includes buildings, vegetation and other surface objects, unlike the DTM.
The current OS Terrain 50 version date is July 2026.
The product covers all of Great Britain.
The product is free OpenData under the OGL.
Supply formats include ASCII Grid, GML, Shapefile, GeoPackage and vector tiles.
The product is updated annually in July.
Grid and contour products are created from the same source data.
Tiled supplies use 10 km by 10 km National Grid tiles.
Tile identifiers quote the south-west National Grid reference.
The grid uses regular 50 metre post spacing.
Each 10 km tile contains 200 columns and 200 rows.
Rows read west to east and progress south.
ASCII heights are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
Grid delivery includes ASC, GML, PRJ, auxiliary styling and metadata files.
XML metadata follows the GEMINI standard.
Metadata is supplied nationally and per tile.
Grid and contour data are interpolated from a source TIN.
A full national grid supply is about 157 MB compressed.
OS OpenData API operations do not require an API key.
The API cannot access previous OpenData releases.
The download endpoint supports National Grid area filtering including TQ.
The automation guide uses product id and version from the product list.
